collocations.meaning: To result in or cause something, usually a consequence.
collocations.example: Poor decisions led ___ failure.

collocations.meaning: To rely on someone or something as necessary for support or a result.
collocations.example: Success often depends ___ hard work.

collocations.meaning: To have something as a consequence or outcome.
collocations.example: The negotiations resulted ___ a new agreement.

collocations.meaning: To trust or depend on someone or something with confidence.
collocations.example: You can always rely ___ her for good advice.

collocations.meaning: To explain or give a reason for something; also, to make up a part or proportion of something.
collocations.example: Bad weather can account ___ the delay.

collocations.meaning: To deal successfully with a difficult situation.
collocations.example: It's not easy to cope ___ so much stress.

collocations.meaning: To be made up of or composed of particular parts.
collocations.example: The committee consists ___ ten members.

collocations.meaning: To take action to solve a problem, or to handle a situation or person.
collocations.example: The manager had to deal ___ several complaints today.

collocations.meaning: To give most of your attention to one particular thing.
collocations.example: Let's focus ___ the most important issue first.

collocations.meaning: To demand something firmly, refusing to accept another option.
collocations.example: She insisted ___ paying for the meal herself.

collocations.meaning: To be convinced that something exists, or to have faith or trust in someone's ability.
collocations.example: I really believe ___ you — you can do this.

collocations.meaning: To make a formal request for something, such as a job or a permit.
collocations.example: He decided to apply ___ the marketing position.

collocations.meaning: To be helped or improved by something.
collocations.example: Many students benefit ___ extra practice before exams.

collocations.meaning: To be affected by an illness or a negative condition over time.
collocations.example: She has been suffering ___ headaches all week.

collocations.meaning: To take part in an activity or event.
collocations.example: All employees are encouraged to participate ___ the training program.

collocations.meaning: To achieve the result you were trying to achieve.
collocations.example: He finally succeeded ___ passing the driving test.

collocations.meaning: To focus your work or study on one particular subject or area.
collocations.example: This law firm specializes ___ international trade disputes.

collocations.meaning: To express an opinion or observation about something.
collocations.example: The critics didn't comment ___ the ending of the film.

collocations.meaning: To direct all your effort or attention toward one thing.
collocations.example: Try to concentrate ___ your breathing to relax.

collocations.meaning: To give something, such as money, effort, or ideas, that helps achieve a result.
collocations.example: Everyone on the team contributed ___ the project's success.

collocations.meaning: To behave or respond in a particular way because of something that happens.
collocations.example: It's hard to predict how people will react ___ the news.

collocations.meaning: To reply or act in answer to something.
collocations.example: The company was slow to respond ___ customer complaints.

collocations.meaning: To change your behavior to suit a new situation or environment.
collocations.example: It took her a while to adapt ___ the new schedule.

collocations.meaning: To be different from or unlike something else.
collocations.example: His opinion differs ___ mine on this issue.

collocations.meaning: To have the same opinion as someone, or to think something is right.
collocations.example: I completely agree ___ your decision.

collocations.meaning: To try to be more successful than another person or company in the same activity.
collocations.example: Small shops struggle to compete ___ big supermarkets.

collocations.meaning: To put money, time, or effort into something, expecting a future benefit.
collocations.example: The company plans to invest ___ new technology next year.

collocations.meaning: To think that someone or something is good, acceptable, or suitable.
collocations.example: Her parents didn't approve ___ her career choice at first.

collocations.meaning: To express disagreement or opposition to something.
collocations.example: Several residents objected ___ the new construction project.

collocations.meaning: To stay in a place or remain ready until someone or something arrives, or until something happens.
collocations.example: We waited ___ the bus for almost an hour.
